newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Digitel gets nod for new rate plans.
newsitem.headline: Digitel gets nod for new rate plans.

text.p: The Philippine's National Telecommunication Commission (NTC) has approved the application of Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc (Digitel) to implement new rates.
Under an NTC order announced on Wednesday, Digitel subscribers will be allowed to choose payment programmes with monthly fees as low as 150 pesos a month to as high as 750 pesos a month.

The higher the monthly fees, the more incentives will accrue to the subscribers in terms of free local and long distance calls. A 750 peso monthly fee, for instance, will mean 800 pesos worth of free local and long distance calls.
Digitel, the telecommunications arm of JG Summit Holdings, is responsible for installing telephone lines in the northern island of Luzon except in the Metro Manila area.

NTC said the new rate schedule is designed to attract users because of its lower monthly fee of 150 pesos. Local subscribers of the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co pay a 250 peso monthly fee while other small private telecom companies charge 220 pesos.
The new rate schedule also provides for an automatic revision of rates to cover any foreign exchange losses, the NTC said.
